correctness.rationale: For every n>=0, BV Stieltjes jump representation and Hilbert triangle inequality reduce the norm to one jump. Parseval gives E_n(t), telescoping Legendre derivatives give E_n'=-P_nP_{n+1} and the exact two-polynomial formula. Simple interlacing identifies local maxima at P_{n+1} zeros. The Sturm energy Phi has derivative -2(n+1)(n+2)t P_{n+1}(t)^2, hence comparison of all positive Gauss zeros is strict. Residual jump functions at distinct t cannot be collinear modulo polynomials, giving all equality cases. Central binomial values and nested-projector monotonicity give the limit. The checker passed 892 independent symbolic/numeric assertions; finite checks are not invoked as the infinite proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Single-jump residuals are equal to a weighted Legendre diagonal kernel, so exact recovery of the claimed result could be phrased as a global weighted-kernel maximum. The paper derives all-degree maximizers by comparing nonadjacent Gauss nodes via a strictly decreasing Sturm energy, then upgrades a one-jump maximum to the exact BV operator norm and all equality cases. None of the inspected source statements explicitly provides that combined classification. Classical special-function identities are credited, not claimed novel.

originality.rationale: After actual public index searches and accessible historical primary-text comparison, no inspected claim determines the all-degree sharp BV-to-L2 Legendre residual norm and its parity-dependent complete extremizer classification. Classical Legendre/CD/Sonin components are acknowledged; closest 2015 Table 1 evaluates only a prescribed jump, and the available cubic result optimizes a different variation-output norm. The inaccessible 1981 article and derivative-based broader theory remain material priority risks.
residual_risks: Full text of Bojanic–Vuilleumier (1981) was not accessible through the available routes; exact coverage was not verified.

Later sharp differentiable-input estimates were accessed only at abstract level; their hypotheses do not visibly include arbitrary BV jumps.

value.rationale: This is a natural sharp, attained, all-degree uniform energy-error benchmark for spectral approximation of arbitrary bounded-variation functions. It classifies all optimal jump locations, reveals a genuinely parity-dependent displacement for every odd degree, provides closed central-binomial constants at every even degree, and gives the exact asymptotic factor 1/sqrt(pi). It is not simply a coefficient bound, one fixed discontinuity or an unmotivated low-degree computation.
